title: T1608.003 — Stage Capabilities - Install Digital Certificate
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Stage Capabilities - Install Digital Certificate with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.
aria: Animated diagram: an attacker registers a lookalike domain, requests a free TLS certificate from an automated certificate authority, clones a login page, phishes an employee who trusts the padlock, and the SOC catches the issuance through public Certificate Transparency logs, blocks the domain and rotates credentials.

nodes.label: Attacker
nodes.tip: The threat actor. Everything on this side happens before any victim is involved.

nodes.label: Lookalike domain
nodes.tip: A freshly registered domain that imitates a supplier portal. The whole operation fronts through it.

nodes.label: Free CA
nodes.tip: A free certificate authority. It issues to anyone who proves control of the domain - including attackers.

nodes.label: Employee
nodes.tip: An office worker. The padlock in the browser is the only trust check many users ever make.

nodes.label: SOC analyst
nodes.tip: The defender. Watches public Certificate Transparency logs and internal logs to catch the fake early.

steps.title: Register the lookalike
steps.caption: The attacker registers vendor-portal-sharepoint[.]top, a name that mixes your supplier portal and brand words. The domain is 0 days old and has no history.
steps.defender: WHOIS and passive DNS record the new registration. If you feed new-domain feeds with your brand vocabulary, this name enters a watchlist today.

detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Ask the free CA
steps.caption: The attacker runs an automated ACME client. It proves control of the domain with a small challenge file and asks a free certificate authority for a TLS certificate. No human is involved.
steps.defender: Nothing inside your network yet. The only public trace is the certificate request pattern, which few defenders watch.

steps.title: Certificate is issued
steps.caption: The free CA issues a 90-day certificate in seconds. The attacker now owns a padlock for a domain that did not exist 3 days ago.
steps.defender: The issuance is written to public Certificate Transparency logs. A CT watchlist or CertStream alert can fire here - the earliest possible warning.

steps.title: Install cert, clone portal
steps.caption: The attacker installs the certificate and serves a copy of the supplier login page. The fake site now shows the same padlock as the real one.
steps.defender: URL scanning services may flag the clone if a crawler visits. Your users see nothing yet.

steps.title: Phish with HTTPS link
steps.caption: A short email tells employees a supplier contract needs approval. The link starts with https:// and shows no warning signs.
steps.defender: The mail gateway sees a URL on a 3-day-old domain. Age-based scoring can hold or flag the message before delivery.

steps.title: Victim clicks and types
steps.caption: The employee clicks, sees the padlock, and enters the supplier portal password. The page forwards them to the real site to reduce suspicion.
steps.defender: First internal evidence: proxy and DNS logs show the fresh domain. TLS SNI logs name it even when the content is encrypted.

detection.detail: A weak signal exists but is not yet a confirmed alert.

steps.title: Harvest and try sign-in
steps.caption: The attacker collects the password and tries to sign in to the real portal from a new country. The password is correct - but MFA blocks the second step.
steps.defender: The identity provider logs a failed sign-in with an impossible-travel pattern. Credential rotation and session revocation go out.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: Block, rotate, report
steps.caption: The SOC blocks the lookalike domain at proxy, DNS, and mail, rotates the user's credentials, and reports the host for take-down.
steps.defender: Hunting finds one click and no further contact. The CT alert that fired days earlier becomes a case-study win: blocked before the phish landed.
